title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
authors: H. Brendan McMahan; Eider Moore; Daniel Ramage; Seth Hampson; Blaise Agüera y Arcas
venue: arXiv preprint (AISTATS 2017 per proceedings; not verified from page)
summary: Introduces federated averaging (FedAvg), local SGD on clients followed by weighted model averaging, and shows it works on image and language tasks with unbalanced, non-IID partitions. The baseline against which all heterogeneity methods in this theme are compared.
note: Reference method; the review names it. Venue (AISTATS 2017) not on the arXiv page read.

title: Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks
authors: Tian Li; Anit Kumar Sahu; Manzil Zaheer; Maziar Sanjabi; Ameet Talwalkar; Virginia Smith
summary: Adds a proximal term to the local objective (FedProx) to limit client drift under statistical and systems heterogeneity, with a convergence analysis. Reports a 22% average absolute test-accuracy gain over FedAvg in highly heterogeneous settings.
note: Seed. Full text saved; abstract states FedProx improves absolute test accuracy by 22% on average over FedAvg in highly heterogeneous settings.

title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
authors: Sai Praneeth Karimireddy; Satyen Kale; Mehryar Mohri; Sashank J. Reddi; Sebastian U. Stich; Ananda Theertha Suresh
summary: Uses control variates (SCAFFOLD) to correct client drift caused by heterogeneous data and shows fewer communication rounds than FedAvg, with convergence that does not depend on how dissimilar the clients are. Published at ICML 2020 (not stated on the page read).
note: Seed. Venue (ICML 2020) not verified from page. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: FedBN: Federated Learning on Non-IID Features via Local Batch Normalization
authors: Xiaoxiao Li; Meirui Jiang; Xiaofei Zhang; Michael Kamp; Qi Dou
summary: Keeps batch-normalisation parameters local and averages the rest (FedBN), targeting feature-shift non-IID such as different scanners; outperforms FedAvg and FedProx on benchmarks including medical images, with a convergence argument in a simplified setting. Direct analogue of a centre-specific offset in the feature distribution.
note: Seed. Full-text PDF saved; only abstract and first pages read.

title: Federated Learning with Non-IID Data
authors: Yue Zhao; Meng Li; Liangzhen Lai; Naveen Suda; Damon Civin; Vikas Chandra
summary: Shows FedAvg accuracy on neural networks falls by up to 55% when each client holds a single class, and proposes sharing a small global data subset to cut this. Early quantification of label-skew harm.
note: Label-skew evidence; natural-image data.

title: Measuring the Effects of Non-Identical Data Distribution for Federated Visual Classification
authors: Tzu-Ming Harry Hsu; Hang Qi; Matthew Brown
summary: Builds synthetic client partitions with a continuous degree of non-identicalness and measures FedAvg degradation on image classification, with a server-momentum mitigation. Gives a controllable heterogeneity protocol that could be used to simulate centres.
note: Natural-image data; included as standard reference on non-IID simulation.

title: Federated Learning on Non-IID Data: A Survey
authors: Hangyu Zhu; Jinjin Xu; Shiqing Liu; Yaochu Jin
venue: arXiv preprint (journal version: Neurocomputing, per web result; not verified)
summary: Survey of how non-IID data affects parametric and non-parametric models in horizontal and vertical federated learning, with the remedies proposed. Useful taxonomy of label, feature and quantity skew.
note: Survey.

title: Non-IID data in Federated Learning: A Survey with Taxonomy, Metrics, Methods, Frameworks and Future Directions
authors: Daniel M. Jimenez G.; David Solans; Mikko Heikkila; Andrea Vitaletti; Nicolas Kourtellis; Aris Anagnostopoulos; Ioannis Chatzigiannakis
summary: Survey that classifies non-IID types, partition protocols and heterogeneity metrics and reviews solutions and frameworks. Supplies metrics to quantify heterogeneity that a simulation of centres could report.
note: Survey; arXiv preprint at time read.

title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
authors: Peter Kairouz; H. Brendan McMahan; Brendan Avent; Aurélien Bellet; Mehdi Bennis; Arjun Nitin Bhagoji; Kallista Bonawitz; Zachary Charles; Graham Cormode; Rachel Cummings; Rafael G. L. D'Oliveira; Hubert Eichner; Salim El Rouayheb; David Evans; Josh Gardner; et al.
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv comment names Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning; volume not verified)
summary: Broad survey of open problems in federated learning, including heterogeneity, personalisation and privacy. Reference for the open-problems framing.
note: Seed from memory [verify]: arXiv comment names Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning; volume/issue text as shown on page is garbled in my parse, check before citing.

title: Personalized Federated Learning: A Meta-Learning Approach
authors: Alireza Fallah; Aryan Mokhtari; Asuman Ozdaglar
summary: Formulates personalised federated learning as finding an initial model that each client adapts with a few gradient steps (Per-FedAvg, MAML-style) and bounds performance by the closeness of client distributions. A route to centre-specific models.
note: Natural-image/benchmark data.

title: Federated Learning with Personalization Layers
authors: Manoj Ghuhan Arivazhagan; Vinay Aggarwal; Aaditya Kumar Singh; Sunav Choudhary
summary: FedPer shares base layers and keeps personalisation layers local to cope with statistical heterogeneity. The shared-body, local-head split is the deep-learning counterpart of centre-specific intercepts or heads.
note: Venue not on page read (arXiv).

title: Exploiting Shared Representations for Personalized Federated Learning
authors: Liam Collins; Hamed Hassani; Aryan Mokhtari; Sanjay Shakkottai
summary: FedRep learns a shared representation across clients and client-specific heads, with convergence for linear representations. The shared-representation/local-head logic matches a shared embedding with centre-specific regressors.
note: ICML 2021 (not verified from page).

title: Ditto: Fair and Robust Federated Learning Through Personalization
authors: Tian Li; Shengyuan Hu; Ahmad Beirami; Virginia Smith
summary: Ditto trains personalised models alongside a global model with a proximal link, giving fairness and robustness under heterogeneity. Personalisation as regularisation toward a global fit.

title: Towards Personalized Federated Learning
authors: Alysa Ziying Tan; Han Yu; Lizhen Cui; Qiang Yang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
summary: Survey of personalised federated learning strategies for heterogeneous data. Organises personalisation into global-model personalisation and learning personalised models.
note: Survey.

title: Personalized Federated Learning through Local Memorization
authors: Othmane Marfoq; Giovanni Neglia; Richard Vidal; Laetitia Kameni
venue: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 162:15070-15092)
summary: Personalises a global model by interpolating with a local k-nearest-neighbour model in the shared embedding space, with a generalisation bound for binary classification. Structurally close to the project's federated reference database concept (C4): local embedding memory plus a global encoder.
verified_from: PMLR page (as returned by web search result)
note: Core candidate for C4 only; classification, not regression.

title: FedMLP: Federated Multi-Label Medical Image Classification under Task Heterogeneity
authors: Zhaobin Sun; Nannan Wu; Junjie Shi; Li Yu; Xin Yang; Kwang-Ting Cheng; Zengqiang Yan
summary: Handles federated multi-label medical image classification where each institution labels only some classes, using pseudo-labels from class prototypes and a global teacher for consistency. Shows partial-label settings can be treated but only for classification.
note: arXiv title read: "FedMLP: Federated Multi-Label Medical Image Classification under Task Heterogeneity".

title: UFPS: A unified framework for partially annotated federated segmentation in heterogeneous data distribution
authors: Le Jiang; Li Yan Ma; Tie Yong Zeng; Shi Hui Ying
summary: Federated segmentation where each site annotates a subset of classes (partial labels), with unified label learning and sharpness-aware optimisation to avoid class collision. Another partial-label treatment, for segmentation.

title: Federated Multi-organ Segmentation with Inconsistent Labels
authors: Xuanang Xu; Hannah H. Deng; Jaime Gateno; Pingkun Yan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging (per arXiv comment: accepted by IEEE Trans...; truncated)
summary: Federated multi-organ segmentation where sites label different organs with little or no overlap. Treats the label-set mismatch explicitly, again for segmentation not regression.
note: Venue truncated in the arXiv comment I parsed; verify.

title: Vertical Federated Learning with Missing Features During Training and Inference
authors: Pedro Valdeira; Shiqiang Wang; Yuejie Chi
summary: Vertical federated learning method (LASER-VFL) that trains and predicts with arbitrary subsets of feature partitions missing. Feature-block missingness for vertical splits; the project's case is horizontal splits with differing output genes.

title: Multimodal Federated Learning With Missing Modalities through Feature Imputation Network
authors: Pranav Poudel; Aavash Chhetri; Prashnna Gyawali; Georgios Leontidis; Binod Bhattarai
summary: Reconstructs bottleneck features of a missing modality with a lightweight network in multimodal federated learning on chest X-ray/report datasets. Modality imputation as a route when clients lack a data type.

title: Learning Reconfigurable Representations for Multimodal Federated Learning with Missing Data
authors: Duong M. Nguyen; Trong Nghia Hoang; Thanh Trung Huynh; Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen; Phi Le Nguyen
summary: Multimodal federated learning where clients observe different modality subsets and also lack some input features, with a reconfigurable representation to align them. Covers both modality and feature missingness.

title: Fed-ReMasker: Federated Tabular Imputation under Feature-Level Missingness
authors: Ioannis Papathanail; Rooholla Poursoleymani; Lubnaa Abdur Rahman; Stavroula Georgia Mougiakakou
summary: Federated tabular imputation for features entirely unobserved at some centres but observed at others, aimed at multi-centre clinical data with partly overlapping feature sets. Abstract-level only: the feature-missing case matches partially overlapping gene panels if genes are treated as columns.
note: arXiv ID 2609 = September 2026; recent preprint. Core candidate for partial feature overlap. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: Handling Covariate Mismatch in Collaborative Linear Prediction
authors: Alexis Ayme; Rémi Khellaf
summary: Studies linear prediction when centres record different covariate sets (blockwise MCAR): a plug-in estimator from aggregated covariance and cross-moment blocks, and an impute-then-ridge scheme in high dimension, with learning rates; only aggregated quantities are exchanged. The closest statistical match found to a summary-statistic ridge head under partial overlap, but the mismatch is in covariates (inputs), not in the response genes.
note: Full-text PDF saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only abstract and introduction read so far. Venue not stated in the pages read.

title: Federated Stain Normalization for Computational Pathology
authors: Nicolas Wagner; Moritz Fuchs; Yuri Tolkach; Anirban Mukhopadhyay
summary: BottleGAN aligns staining styles across laboratories and is trained federatedly with knowledge distillation on a shared public reference set; reported 42% IoU gain over federated baselines on a multi-institution set per a secondary summary page (not in abstract). Requires a shareable reference dataset on the server.
note: Full-text PDF saved; abstract and the MICCAI review page read. The 42% IoU figure is from a third-party summary and is unverified.

title: A Federated Learning System for Histopathology Image Analysis With an Orchestral Stain-Normalization GAN
authors: Yiqing Shen; Arcot Sowmya; Yulin Luo; Xiaoyao Liang; Dinggang Shen; Jing Ke
summary: Federated stain-style normalisation with one orchestrating generator and distributed discriminators plus temporal self-distillation; downstream federated classification accuracy rises by over 20% against the baseline classifier and approaches centralised training.

title: FedSDA: Federated Stain Distribution Alignment for Non-IID Histopathological Image Classification
authors: Cheng-Chang Tsai; Kai-Wen Cheng; Chun-Shien Lu
venue: arXiv preprint (AAAI 2026 version: DOI 10.1609/aaai.v40i12.37918; Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 40(12):9566-9575)
summary: Aligns each client's stain distribution to a target by stain separation and a diffusion model on stain matrices trained without raw images, improving existing federated baselines on non-IID histopathology classification. Seed FedSDA.
note: Same work as AAAI paper (AAAI page via web search; ojs.aaai.org not directly reachable). Full-text PDF of arXiv extended version saved; abstract and method intro read.

title: FedStain: Modeling Higher-Order Stain Statistics for Federated Domain Generalization in Computational Pathology
authors: Fengyi Zhang; Junya Zhang; Wenzhuo Sun
summary: FedStain models higher-order stain statistics for federated domain generalisation; on Camelyon17 and a scanner-defined MvMidog-Fed benchmark it beats FedAvg, FedProx and federated DG baselines by up to 3.9 points absolute accuracy.
note: Full-text PDF saved; abstract and introduction skimmed.

title: FedHisto-PAST: Parameter-Efficient Stain-Aware Federated Learning for Cross-Site Lung Histopathology Classification
authors: Muhammad Muhtasim Shahriar; M. M. Golam Hafiz; Saad Aloteibi; Mohammad Ali Moni
summary: Five-client non-IID simulation for lung histology classification using a frozen HIBOU-B foundation model with parameter-efficient adaptation, stain-conditioned consistency and prototype learning. Relevant because it federates on a frozen pathology foundation model under stain shift.
note: Submitted preprint (Engineering Applications of AI per arXiv comment). Full-text PDF saved; abstract read only.

title: Federated Distillation for Whole Slide Image via Gaussian-Mixture Feature Alignment and Curriculum Integration
authors: Luru Jing; Cong Cong; Yanyuan Chen; Yongzhi Cao
summary: FedHD handles institutions with different MIL architectures and feature extractors by exchanging locally distilled synthetic feature representations instead of model parameters. Addresses encoder heterogeneity across centres on whole-slide data.

title: Scanner-Induced Domain Shifts Undermine the Robustness of Pathology Foundation Models
authors: Erik Thiringer; Fredrik K. Gustafsson; Kajsa Ledesma Eriksson; Mattias Rantalainen
summary: Evaluates 14 pathology foundation models on 384 breast cancer slides scanned on five scanners, finding all encode scanner-specific variation in embeddings and shift calibration even when AUC is stable. Direct evidence that frozen-encoder embeddings carry a scanner offset.
note: Not federated; core candidate because the project federates heads on frozen foundation-model embeddings. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: Self-supervised stain normalization empowers privacy-preserving and model generalization in digital pathology
authors: Jianhang Wang; Jiahui Yu; Haixu Yang; Yunqi Zhu; Lei Jiang; Xiaoxiao Li; Jing Zhang; Yingke Xu
summary: Self-supervised stain lookup table (StainLUT) normalises stain at a centre without cross-centre data transfer and gives cross-centre tumour localisation and classification comparable to centralised models.
note: Open access status inferred from npj Digital Medicine; not checked.

title: PathFL: Multi-alignment Federated Learning for pathology image segmentation
authors: Yuan Zhang; Feng Chen; Yaolei Qi; Guanyu Yang; Huazhu Fu
summary: PathFL aligns image style, features and aggregation across clients for pathology segmentation on four heterogeneous collections spanning source, modality, organ and scanner variation. Reports gains over federated baselines (sizes not in the part of the abstract read).

title: Cross-institutional HER2 assessment via a computer-aided system using federated learning and stain composition augmentation
authors: C Yang; Y Chen; S Chang; Y Hsieh; Y Hung; Y Lin; Y Lee; C Lin; Y Lin; Y Lu; Y Lin
summary: Federated HER2 assessment with a stain-composition augmentation, trained across a Taiwan hospital set and a public set; accuracy above 90% at both sites, 30% better generalisation than a single-site baseline, and similar to pooled training.
note: Author list on the Europe PMC record is given as initials only (PPR790472).

title: Siloed Federated Learning for Multi-Centric Histopathology Datasets
authors: Mathieu Andreux; Jean Ogier du Terrail; Constance Beguier; Eric W. Tramel
summary: Local-statistic batch-normalisation layers for multi-centre histopathology federation give centre-specific models robust to heterogeneity. Early pathology use of the FedBN idea.

title: FedDG: Federated Domain Generalization on Medical Image Segmentation via Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space
authors: Quande Liu; Cheng Chen; Jing Qin; Qi Dou; Pheng-Ann Heng
summary: Federated domain generalisation (FedDG) shares amplitude-spectrum information across sites so the model generalises to unseen hospitals in medical segmentation. Targets new-centre deployment rather than within-federation fit.

title: Flexible and scalable federated learning with deep feature prompts for digital pathology
authors: Cong Cong; Yang Song; Antonio Di Ieva; Angela Chou; Anthony J. Gill; Enrico Coiera; Sidong Liu
summary: Federated Deep Feature Prompting: clients share small prompts applied to patch embeddings from whole-slide images, cutting communication by over 99.9% with mean AUC gains of 0.11-0.13 over local-only training and up to 0.10 over the strongest federated method on TCGA-IDH and CAMELYON16/17. A frozen-feature federated route.
note: Seed (Cong et al.). Classification, not expression. Crossref: npj Digital Medicine 9:578. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: Proportionally Fair Hospital Collaborations in Federated Learning of Histopathology Images
authors: S. Maryam Hosseini; Milad Sikaroudi; Morteza Babaie; H. R. Tizhoosh
summary: Proportionally fair federated objective that narrows performance gaps between hospitals; evaluated on two histopathology and two general datasets for speed, accuracy and fairness.
note: Seed. Fairness across centres as heterogeneity outcome.

title: Federated learning for computational pathology on gigapixel whole slide images
authors: Ming Y. Lu; Richard J. Chen; Dehan Kong; Jana Lipkova; Rajendra Singh; Drew F.K. Williamson; Tiffany Y. Chen; Faisal Mahmood
summary: Federated weakly supervised attention MIL on gigapixel slides with differential privacy on two diagnostic tasks and survival prediction using thousands of slides. Shows slide-label federated learning is feasible.
note: Seed. Seed DOI form media.2022.102298 does not resolve; resolving DOI is 10.1016/j.media.2021.102298 (vol 76, art. 102298, 2022).

title: Federated learning and differential privacy for medical image analysis
authors: Mohammed Adnan; Shivam Kalra; Jesse C. Cresswell; Graham W. Taylor; Hamid R. Tizhoosh
summary: Differentially private federated learning on TCGA histology with IID and non-IID splits and varying hospital numbers; private distributed training approaches conventional performance.
note: Seed. Non-IID simulated from one public repository.

title: Swarm learning for decentralized artificial intelligence in cancer histopathology
authors: Oliver Lester Saldanha; Philip Quirke; Nicholas P. West; Jacqueline A. James; Maurice B. Loughrey; Heike I. Grabsch; Manuel Salto-Tellez; Elizabeth Alwers; Didem Cifci; Narmin Ghaffari Laleh; Tobias Seibel; Richard Gray; Gordon G. A. Hutchins; Hermann Brenner; Marko van Treeck; et al.
summary: Swarm learning over three cohorts (Northern Ireland, Germany, US; over 5,000 patients) to predict BRAF and MSI from H&E. Multi-site practice with real cohort differences.
note: Seed; mainly other themes.

title: A review on federated learning in computational pathology
authors: Lydia A. Schoenpflug; Yao Nie; Fahime Sheikhzadeh; Viktor H. Koelzer
summary: Review of 15 federated learning studies in computational pathology: aggregation methods give 0-3% gains, domain alignment 4-20%, privacy measures cost 0.2-6%. Quantitative summary of what heterogeneity handling buys in pathology.
note: Core candidate: aggregates evidence for domain alignment.

title: Federated Learning for Histopathology Image Classification: A Systematic Review
authors: Meriem Touhami; Mohammad Faizal Ahmad Fauzi; Zaka Ur Rehman; Sarina Mansor
summary: PRISMA systematic review of 24 federated histopathology classification studies (2020-2025): methods, datasets, metrics, challenges.

title: Batch effects can impair federated learning in multi-center omics studies
authors: Yuliya Burankova; Julian Klemm; Jens J. G. Lohmann; Anne Hartebrodt; Ahmad Taheri; Niklas Probul; Jan Baumbach; Olga Zolotareva
summary: Shows uncorrected batch effects degrade federated k-means and random forest on four multi-centre omics sets, and introduces fedRBE, a federated limma removeBatchEffect with secure aggregation that handles missing values and non-identical feature sets across clients. Closest found to a batch-offset correction applicable to centres with different measured features.
note: Seed (fedRBE). Preprint; PDF saved; abstract and introduction read.

title: Harmony-based data integration for distributed single-cell multi-omics data
authors: Ruizhi Yuan; Ziqi Rong; Haoran Hu; Tianhao Liu; Shiyue Tao; Wei Chen; Lu Tang
summary: Federated Harmony integrates decentralised single-cell data without sharing raw data and matches centralised Harmony.
note: Seed. Title is "Harmony-based data integration for distributed single-cell multi-omics data"; "Federated Harmony" is the method name. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: FedscGen: privacy-preserving federated batch effect correction of single-cell RNA sequencing data
authors: Mohammad Bakhtiari; Stefan Bonn; Fabian Theis; Olga Zolotareva; Jan Baumbach
summary: FedscGen federates scGen batch correction with secure multiparty computation, matching scGen on NMI, ASW, kBET and related metrics on Human Pancreas data, with integration of new studies.
note: Found by search, not in scan. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: scFed: federated learning for cell type classification with scRNA-seq
authors: Shuang Wang; Bochen Shen; Lanting Guo; Mengqi Shang; Jinze Liu; Qi Sun; Bairong Shen
summary: scFed benchmarks four cell-type classifiers within a federated framework on eight scRNA-seq datasets with accuracy competitive with centralised models.
note: Seed. Crossref year 2023 (online); seed said 2024 25(1).

title: SwarmMAP: swarm learning for decentralized cell type annotation in single cell sequencing data
authors: Oliver Lester Saldanha; Vivien Goepp; Kevin Pfeiffer; Hyojin Kim; Jie Fu Zhu; Rafael Kramann; Sikander Hayat; Jakob Nikolas Kather
summary: SwarmMAP uses swarm learning for decentralised cell-type annotation with F1 of 0.93, 0.98 and 0.88 in heart, lung and breast data.
note: Seed. Crossref: vol 12, art. 41. Preprint 10.1101/2025.01.13.632775 also exists.

title: A comprehensive experimental comparison between federated and centralized learning
authors: Swier Garst; Julian Dekker; Marcel Reinders
summary: Systematic comparison of federated and centralised learning over classifiers and datasets with varied sample and class distributions: similar performance in most settings, but sensitivity to batch effects that coincide with site.
note: Core candidate: batch effects confounded with site. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; excerpts read: authors z-normalised each gene locally (batch-correction-like) before federated PCA on datasets from different technologies, after which federated and central classifiers performed similarly.

title: Federated Learning Performance Depends on Site Variation in Global HIV Data Consortia
authors: Nicholas J. Jackson; Chao Yan; Yanink Caro-Vega; Fabio Paredes; Ronaldo Ismerio Moreira; Stanley Cadet; Diana Varela; Carina Cesar; Stephany N Duda; Bryan E. Shepherd; Bradley A. Malin
summary: Federated HIV prediction across six sites in five countries (22,234 people) approached centralised performance and beat site-only models; gains varied with site size and between-site heterogeneity, and local fine-tuning sometimes helped.
note: Tabular clinical data; preprint. Full text saved; excerpts read: in one site (Haiti) adding other sites lowered performance, and in simulation FedAvg and FedProx did worse under between-site heterogeneity.

title: Federated Mixed Effects Logistic Regression Based on One‐Time Shared Summary Statistics
authors: Marie Analiz April Limpoco; Christel Faes; Niel Hens
summary: Estimates a mixed-effects logistic regression from summary statistics shared once, by generating pseudo-data that match them. One-shot summary sharing can carry random site effects.
note: Found by search.

title: Unlocking multi-institutional insights into disease progression with PEAL as a lossless, one-shot federated learning solution
authors: Yicheng Shen; Ji Soo Kim; Chongliang Luo; Scott L. Zeger; Robyn T. Domsic; Ami A. Shah; Jiayi Tong
summary: PEAL fits multilevel linear mixed models from a single round of summary statistics and reproduces the pooled analysis, applied to systemic sclerosis cohorts.
note: Exact pooled equivalence is the abstract claim.

title: FedGMMAT: Federated generalized linear mixed model association tests
authors: Wentao Li; Han Chen; Xiaoqian Jiang; Arif Harmanci
summary: FedGMMAT federates generalised linear mixed model association tests with random effects for heterogeneous samples while genotype data stay local.

title: Federated generalized linear mixed models for collaborative genome-wide association studies
authors: Wentao Li; Han Chen; Xiaoqian Jiang; Arif Harmanci
summary: dMEGA federates mixed-effects association testing with a reference projection that corrects population stratification across sites.

title: Learning from electronic health records across multiple sites: A communication-efficient and privacy-preserving distributed algorithm
authors: Rui Duan; Mary Regina Boland; Zixuan Liu; Yue Liu; Howard H Chang; Hua Xu; Haitao Chu; Christopher H Schmid; Christopher B Forrest; John H Holmes; Martijn J Schuemie; Jesse A Berlin; Jason H Moore; Yong Chen
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association 27(3):376-385
summary: ODAL: one-shot distributed logistic regression using first- and second-order gradient information from other sites, close to the pooled estimate in simulation.
note: Seed (Duan et al.), logistic regression only.

title: Targeting underrepresented populations in precision medicine: A federated transfer learning approach
authors: Sai Li; Tianxi Cai; Rui Duan
summary: FETA integrates heterogeneous populations by federated transfer learning, matching pooled analysis with few communication rounds and analysing heterogeneity, communication budget and privacy.
note: Seed (Li, Cai, Duan 2023).

title: High resolution mapping of the tumor microenvironment using integrated single-cell, spatial and in situ analysis
authors: Amanda Janesick; Robert Shelansky; Andrew D. Gottscho; Florian Wagner; Stephen R. Williams; Morgane Rouault; Ghezal Beliakoff; Carolyn A. Morrison; Michelli F. Oliveira; Jordan T. Sicherman; Andrew Kohlway; Jawad Abousoud; Tingsheng Yu Drennon; Seayar H. Mohabbat; 10x Development Teams; et al.
summary: Combines Visium, Xenium and single-cell data on FFPE breast cancer; per the Nature Communications page, Xenium probes 313 genes against whole-transcriptome Visium and has about 8-fold higher per-gene sensitivity in the shared area. Concrete example of platform-specific panels.
note: Panel/sensitivity numbers read from the journal page via web search.

title: Evidence of off-target probe binding in the 10x Genomics Xenium v1 Human Breast Gene Expression Panel compromises accuracy of spatial transcriptomic profiling
authors: C Hallinan; HJ Ji; SL Salzberg; J Fan
summary: Predicts off-target probe binding for at least 21 of 280 genes in a Xenium breast panel and shows some genes' patterns mirror off-target genes against Visium CytAssist. Gene-level platform bias is a source of gene-specific offsets.
note: The eLife reviewed-preprint version reports 14 of 313 genes; counts differ by version.

title: SpatialBench : Comparative cross-platform benchmarking of high-resolution spatial transcriptomics using matched mouse lymphoid tissue
authors: Ashleigh Solano; Raymond K. H. Yip; Changqing Wang; Daniela Amann-Zalcenstein; Pradeep Rajasekhar; Ishrat Zaman; Allan Motyer; Marek Cmero; Yang Xu; Yining Pan; Casey J. A. Anttila; Stephanie I. Studniberg; Peter F. Hickey; Layla Wang; Callum J. Sargeant; et al.
summary: Matched Visium HD, Xenium and MERSCOPE profiling of mouse spleen; the text page shows Visium HD correlating best with snRNA-seq (R=0.92 over 14,999 genes) against 0.64 for Xenium on ~100 genes, with only 90 genes shared across platforms.
note: Numbers from full-text page returned by web search.

title: A technical comparison of spatial transcriptomics platforms across six cancer types
authors: Sergi Cervilla; Daniela Grases; Elena Perez; Francisco X. Real; Eva Musulen; Julieta Aprea; Manel Esteller; Eduard Porta-Pardo
summary: Benchmarks Visium v1, v2, HD, Xenium and CosMx on matched FFPE tumours, including Xenium Multi-Tissue (377 genes) against Xenium Prime (5,000 genes). Documents panel-size and platform differences in transcript recovery on the same samples.
note: Found via OpenReview-worded web search.

title: Resolving sensitivity, specificity and signal contamination in Xenium spatial transcriptomics
authors: Mariia Bilous; Daria Buszta; Jonathan Bac; Senbai Kang; Yixing Dong; Stephanie Tissot; Sylvie Andre; Marina Alexandre Gaveta; Christel Voize; Solange Peters; Krisztian Homicsko; Raphael Gottardo
summary: Over 40 breast and lung tumour sections profiled with diverse Xenium panels; targeted panels are more sensitive than the 5K panel, and shared genes across panels correlate reasonably. Panel choice changes per-gene signal.
note: Found via web search.

title: PPML-Omics: A privacy-preserving federated machine learning method protects patients’ privacy in omic data
authors: Juexiao Zhou; Siyuan Chen; Yulian Wu; Haoyang Li; Bin Zhang; Longxi Zhou; Yan Hu; Zihang Xiang; Zhongxiao Li; Ningning Chen; Wenkai Han; Chencheng Xu; Di Wang; Xin Gao
summary: Decentralised differentially private federated learning on omics data from three sequencing technologies. The abstract does not describe differing gene panels or centre offsets.
note: Seed (PPML-Omics); context for another theme.

title: Benchmarking the translational potential of spatial gene expression prediction from histology
authors: Chuhan Wang; Adam S. Chan; Xiaohang Fu; Shila Ghazanfar; Jinman Kim; Ellis Patrick; Jean Y. H. Yang
summary: Benchmark of eleven histology-to-spatial-expression methods on five datasets with external TCGA validation, including generalisability. The abstract gives no cross-study transfer numbers.
note: Seed. "Weak transfer across studies" is not stated in the abstract; needs full text.

title: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Cross-Modal Learning for Histology and Gene Expression in Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Rushin H. Gindra; Giovanni Palla; Mathias Nguyen; Sophia J. Wagner; Manuel Tran; Fabian J Theis; Dieter Saur; Lorin Crawford; Tingying Peng
summary: HESCAPE benchmarks cross-modal pretraining on a pan-organ set spanning six gene panels and 54 donors; contrastive pretraining helps mutation classification but degrades direct expression prediction versus baseline encoders. Direct evidence on multi-panel data from one benchmark.
note: Seed. Found via web search; how panels are handled needs full text. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: Personalised Federated Learning On Heterogeneous Feature Spaces
authors: Alain Rakotomamonjy; Maxime Vono; Hamlet Jesse Medina Ruiz; Liva Ralaivola
summary: FLIC maps each client's differently defined features into a common space via local embeddings and federated Wasserstein barycentres, for personalised FL with heterogeneous feature spaces.
note: Found via OpenReview-worded web search; venue not on page read. Full text saved to fedlearn_papers/T5; only excerpts read so far.

title: Federated Learning with Heterogeneous and Private Label Sets
authors: Adam Breitholtz; Edvin Listo Zec; Fredrik D. Johansson
summary: Studies federated learning when clients hold different, possibly private, label sets; fewer labels per client harm all methods substantially, and centralised tuning helps at the cost of variance.
note: Found via web search; classification labels.

title: Why Batch Normalization Damage Federated Learning on Non-IID Data?
authors: Yanmeng Wang; Qingjiang Shi; Tsung-Hui Chang
summary: Argues batch normalisation harms federated learning on non-IID data and proposes FedTAN, aggregating BN statistics and gradients.
note: Natural images.

title: Overcoming the Challenges of Batch Normalization in Federated Learning
authors: Rachid Guerraoui; Rafael Pinot; Geovani Rizk; John Stephan; François Taiani
summary: Federated batch normalisation (FBN) makes BN statistics consistent with centralised training, reducing external covariate shift.
note: Natural images.

title: BN-SCAFFOLD: controlling the drift of Batch Normalization statistics in Federated Learning
authors: Gonzalo Iñaki Quintana; Laurence Vancamberg; Vincent Jugnon; Mathilde Mougeot; Agnès Desolneux
summary: BN-SCAFFOLD controls drift of BN statistics under heterogeneous FL at lower communication cost than FedTAN.
note: Natural images.

title: UniFed: A Unified Framework for Federated Learning on Non-IID Image Features
authors: Meirui Jiang; Xiaoxiao Li; Xiaofei Zhang; Michael Kamp; Qi Dou

note: Natural images.

title: Rethinking Normalization Methods in Federated Learning
authors: Zhixu Du; Jingwei Sun; Ang Li; Pin-Yu Chen; Jianyi Zhang; Hai "Helen" Li; Yiran Chen
summary: Shows BN causes external covariate shift in federated learning and that layer normalisation avoids it.
note: Natural images.

title: Multi-site fMRI Analysis Using Privacy-preserving Federated Learning and Domain Adaptation: ABIDE Results
authors: Xiaoxiao Li; Yufeng Gu; Nicha Dvornek; Lawrence Staib; Pamela Ventola; James S. Duncan
summary: Multi-site fMRI analysis with federated learning and domain adaptation on ABIDE; an example of site effects in a multi-site medical imaging federation.
note: Neuroimaging.

authors: Haolong Jin; Shenglin Liu; Cong Cong; Qingmin Feng; Yongzhi Liu; Lina Huang; Yingzi Hu
summary: FedWSIDD federates whole-slide classification via dataset distillation to cope with heterogeneous compute across institutions. Same work as the MICCAI 2025 page.

title: Hybrid Batch Normalisation: Resolving the Dilemma of Batch Normalisation in Federated Learning
authors: Hongyao Chen; Tianyang Xu; Xiaojun Wu; Josef Kittler
summary: Proposes Hybrid Batch Normalisation to resolve BN degradation under non-IID federated learning.
note: Abstract read from PMLR page.

title: Harnessing Heterogeneous Statistical Strength for Personalized Federated Learning via Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
authors: Mahendra Singh Thapa; Rui Li
summary: Hierarchical Bayesian inference for personalised FL that aggregates personalised posteriors without the biases of heuristic averaging. Hierarchical (random-effect-like) structure across clients.

title: FedFed: Feature Distillation against Data Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
authors: Zhiqin Yang; Yonggang Zhang; Yu Zheng; Xinmei Tian; Hao Peng; Tongliang Liu; Bo Han

note: Natural-image benchmarks.
